Quote: Arachnid, 2006-12-18T07:51:43Z
One half-baked idea that's occurred to me is a friends-based rating system. You indicate who your 'friends' are on NUMA - those you trust - and ratings are calculated individually for you, weighting votes by your friends most highly, followed by votes by their friends, and so on. This has several issues, though, mostly technical:
- Requires implementation of a social networking style 'friends' system.
- There's no single 'leaderboard' people can refer to. You can no longer say you're "in the top 10".
- There'd need to be some default for when you're not logged in, which may just become the current system all over again.
- Since ratings have to be calculated in a fairly involved manner, and will vary for every person that's viewing them, there are potential implications for system load. Calculating a top-rated list would be even worse.

THat would be pretty sweet, but, as you mentioned, the calculations would be endless.

My question is what if you have no friends?

1. If somebody bugs or "snipes" (gives you a zero and leaves) you, on the forums or not, just stay on the down-low. Keep cool, and just laugh. They want attention, and if you give it to them...you basically stoop down to their level. Or you could do what I do...which is saying as a comment in my maps "oh, wow, sniper, you sure got me..."

5. Any questions, remember to FIRST AND FOREMOST return to the FAQ's.

That is all.

Well, Im just about on the younger side of the general majority of you guys. Not like under twelve, but I am at the age that people find it cool to go out with one another. For me, the concept of 'cool' isn't exactly appealing. The only thing I want dealing with a social life is a group of good friends who would never and could never back out on me at the last second. Like that would ever happen. I am a NERD. I can never deny that. I get straight A's, I take classes higher than anyone else in my year, and the only class I have gotten a B in in any of the quarters was P.E, and although that was because of a mathematical error, it still is on my record. I have never gone out with anyone, nor have I been asked. Im not sure if it's a good thing or not. I sorta want to laugh at the people who are going out, yet I feel a curious jealous feeling pulling at me. But the horrible thing is the expectations put on me. I know I dont want to work my hardest. I know it deep down to the bone. I only like working if I am interested in the topic, and now, I am losing my interest in the thing that is the most vital for me. That is math. I am three years above what I am supposed to be in math, and I am taking the class as an honors course. So basically, I will need to spend day and night on something I dont want to work on. And I will be expected to get an A. I know I can do it, it's just that Im afraid I wont work hard enough. I never do. It's really weird.

Apart from all of that school jibber-jabber, there is my actual personality. Like I said, all I want are friends who I can trust, and who can trust me with their lives. I actually probably have a couple of those. The more that people know me, the more they seem to like me. Although, that said, no girl would ever dare ask me out, because if they do, their social life will be down the drain. I am at the bottom of the social circle. Either way, my personality seems to be good. All who know me seem to think I am kind. I am very religious, but I am not a Christian. Nor a Muslim. Nor a Hindu. I am not Buddhist. I am a Baha'i, a religion that is not known very well. I spend hours of my weeks doing Baha'i related tasks, such as teaching children's classes and praying and reading Baha'i books. Laugh if you want, but I have really PRAYED for some of you. Not really for a reason, but because you seemed down, or something. Either way, that is that.

And then there is my family life. That couldnt be going much better. My mom and dad are perfectly happy with each other. My brother and I are perfeclty happy with each other (in a different way), but my brother will be going off to college pretty soon, which will be a big blow to me. Oh well. I only have a couple of years after him. Either way, if I was to grade my life, it would look like this: Social life: F. School (work) life: A-. Personality: A-. Religion: A. Family:A. So, off of that, I will average it out at an A-, considering I really dont care about the social thing. My life is good, and I think that so long as you can still keep standing, or at least still keep fighting for what you believe in, deep down, you can make it no matter what.

What: The Metanet Love Game was first made in 2006. I will be doing it once every year from now on. It is basically a compatibility test to see who you should be friends with in this forums, and who you shouldnt be friends with. But it is not one hundred percent true.
When: Right now, and it ends September 30
Why: For fun. That's just about it.
Who: Everyone, including me this time, that wants to.
Spoiler: FAQ'sWhy bother wasting my time doing this?
If you have that kind of an attitude, then just don't do it, or get a friend from the forums to do it with you. The sky is the limit. That, and I can only handle 100 PM's.

What exactly do you have to do?
Type in letters next to numbers. Read the rules for more info.

Is it easy?
Yes

Will metanembers, mods, and admin get a longer time to complete it?
Yes, they will have until October, because most of them are old enough that they might have something better to do until then, and because I wont be done by then anyways.

RULES:

You must follow all of these rules, or your votes will be thrown out, and you will receive a PM to redo them, or just drop out of the Game. Just so you know, the last response is generally a joke.

1. You MUST post your answers next to the numbers, ie:
1: A
2: D
3: G

and so on. If I get a post that just is filled up with letters, I am not going to bother checking it, because it will take WAYYYY too long.

2. IF YOU DO NOT HAVE AN ANSWER TO ONE OF THE QUESTIONS, or none of the answers fit you, type in the number 1. I dont care. The number 1 is for those questions that you cant answer.

3. You must have everything turned in by NOVEMBER 31. or else it gets thrown away. No half-completed quizzes will be accepted.

Grading: AND THIS PART WAS EDITED ON OCTOBER 6

You can get up to a hundred points with any random person.

0-20: You two will never get along
21-30: You could be friends
31-40: You guys can probably get along fine
41-50: Very likely the best of friends
51-60: Obviously the best of friends
61-70: That is a lot. You guys could get along like trees and dirt.
71-80: You guys are almost exactly like each other, or you rigged it.
81-90: Wow. I dont believe it. You guys totally rigged this.
91-95: You guys rigged it. That's it.
96-99: Cheaters
100: H4X0RR3RZZZZ

If you get a decimal, round it up.

#17076 1 2007-09-03T19:07:33Z Turtle
Basically, this is an experience point game. Yes, I know that these are overused, and yet I am still using them. Basically, you will be choosing a character type to play as, and, if you want, you can form allies. That is where it gets interesting.

Rules:

1. Before you join, you must PM me
2. You can join any time you like, but you must start with the lowest stats possible.
3. WHEN YOU FORM ALLIES, BOTH YOU AND THE ALLY LEADER MUST PM ME TELLING ME. BOTH OF YOU.
4. The team leader is chosen, at first, by the two or so people who start the ally, and then will be chosen later by the person with the highest stats. If you die, then you will start all over with the same stats you had in the beginning, unless if you want to change your character.
5. We will not start until I get at least two groups (or a group and a person), so whoever starts off will have a better chance at surviving if you start from the beginning.
6. ABSOULUTELY NO DOUBLE POSTING unless if your name is turtle.
7. Every time you post, you must attack, or buy something from me, or at least do something that is not spam, or you will lose five points. This is because of the long-lasting pain that will reach people. See below for more details. Backstabbing your team is allowed. However, your team captain will likely kick you off if you do. I realise you can ruin the entire game by doing this.

How does it work?
Basically, you have two different attacks, and a certain amount of defense. I will be playing, but I am the medicine man/the marketer. So if you get poisoned and need help, or if you are just cut and need a bandaid, you need to come to me and give me a certain amount of your 'experience' in order for you to not die. If you end up not coming to me within a certain amount of posts, you will find that you lose one or more health for every post, or every other post, or so, depending on your health problem.

What are things that will cause me to go to the medicine man?

Easy to cure, not hard to fix

Small cut: you need a bandaid. Every five posts that you dont get one, you lose one health point.

Broken bone: You need a cast. Every two posts that you dont get one, you lose a point.

Stubbed toe: You need an ice pack. Every four posts that you dont get one, you lose one health point

Temporary blindness: You need shades. You can keep shades, but you may not share them. Every two posts that you dont get one, you lose a point, and your team captain loses a point. If you are the team captain, you lose two points.

Temporary deafness: You need to either stay out of this thing for a WEEK, or you need to pay me.

Itchiness: You need skin cream. You can use skin cream five times in total, or share it, so long as the total is five. You lose a point every three posts if you fail to apply the cream. And if you want to use someone else's, you must first ask me.

Medium, can be dangerous
(You ought to PM me to insure that I dont forget about this if you want to stay alive with these)

Open cut: You lose a point for every post until you get a bandaid.

Bad breath: Everyone on your ally loses a point for every five posts until you get a pack of breathmints. Or you buy mint gum, but that is more expensive.

Stuffy nose: May turn into a cold if you don't buy enough liquids.

Bad hair day: Will cause temporary blindness to somebody in your group every five posts until you buy a comb, which you can keep, but you cannot share.

Sliver: you lose five points for every four posts unless if you buy tweezers which you can keep, but cannot share.

Confusion: every other attack that you throw will hurt someone on your own team, so you should buy a TV, which will be useful for your ENTIRE group because you can all use it.

Deadly Diseases:
(you are probably going to be dead if you get these early on in the game)

Common cold: You need cough sirrup. It only works once, and only you can use it. Every post that you dont have it, you lose a point. Every other post, you lose a point, AND one of your team members gets it. Just imagine how this thing can multiply, so you need to buy cough sirrup quickly.

Open wound (large): You need a BIG bandaid. Otherwise, you lose one post after two turns, and it doubles for every other turn until you die.

Spinal/cranial damage: You are out for a week unless if you buy surgery, which takes a day. And if you are out for a week, imagine what your opponents can do to you.

Poison: You need an antidote, or you lose three points every turn. If you have an antidote bought already, you dont need to say that you are using it.

THERE ARE MORE, BUT THESE ARE THE ONES I HAVE DOWN FOR NOW.

PLAYERS:

These are the people you have to choose from so far. The ones that are locked say *lock* on them.

Plumber:
Attack: 12
Defense: 12
Money: 6

This person is useful if peope decide to attack your fort (or home), because he can fix it.

Architect:
Attack: 5
Defense: 15
Money: 10

This person is vital if you want to be able to come back alive, because otherwise you dont get a home.

Engineer:
Attack: 8
Defense: 11
Money: 11

This person is nice to have around, because he can ask me to invent a new item to help you (for example, a container that can hold enough of something to last your entire team a while), and then I can add it to the store and give you guys an item of it for free.

Burgular:
Attack: 1
Defense: 21
Money: 8

This guy can steal anything. Unless if you PM me to buy a device to hold him back. I say PM so he doesn't know. However, he may be able to get around it...

Teacher:
Attack: 8
Defense: 8
Money: 14

The teacher can teach people how to make swords out of sticks that you buy at the market, but only if the teacher buys lessons first. So basically, as soon as the teacher learns how to do something with a weapon at the market, you can all buy it. But only if you are on the same team.

Lawyer:
Attack: 3
Defense: 11
Money: 16

This guy can keep on earning money if he can suggest something to me. So if you find any problems with this, tell your lawyer, and he can tell me, thus earning you money.

*lock* Politician:
Attack: 8
Defense: 2
Money: 25

For this guy, you may want to get security. But he is good because he has money.

*lock* Bodyguard:
Attack: 15
Defense: 20
Money: 0

This guy is essential because is the only guy who can litterally transfer his stats to anyone of his choice. Which means that he can give life to dead people. He is the only one that can go through life-giving surgery to give him 20 defense when he dies. but that costs a lot...

*lock* Doctor:
Attack: 5
Defense: 10
Money: 20
Healing: +

Basically, he can heal you. That's right. Free surgery for no cost. But he has to ask the medicine man first.

*lock* Military fighter:
Attack: 25
Defense: 10
Money: 5

You will see how fun it is to be this guy with the doctor in the same ally when you get that far.

*lock* Keron:
Attack: 15
Defense: 15
Money: 15

One of the best fighters.

*lock* Tsukatu:
Attack: 30
Defense: 15
Money: 0

This guy can steal, just like the burgular. So if you start as the burgular, and you get enough money for an upgrade, become Tsukatu.

*lock* Arachnid:
Attack: 10
Defense: 25
Money: 10

This guy helps because if you have him and Keron together, then you can go on to become...

*SUPERlock* Warrior:
Attack: 25
Defense: 40
Money: 25

Yeah. This guy's attack can defeat anyone at starting. And it would take multiple attacks to bring him down. Beat that.

*SUPERlock* Mare/Raigan (whichever you want to be. They are the same)
Attack: 0
Defense: 50
Money: 5

These guys come into effect whenever you want. If you are the leader of a 10+ person ally, than you can play as one of them. But is it really worth it? They DO get automatic discounts at the store...

*SUPERlock* Priest:

Attack: 20
Defense: 20
Money: 100

Do I even need to say why you might want this guy?

*SUPERlock* President:
Attack: 20
Defense: 5
Money: 50

Only the leader of a group, or a soloist, can upgrade to this. Although he may seem peothetic, he can veto an attack, saying why it is unjust, and I may or may not listen.

THINGS TO BUY AT THE MARKET, OR FROM THE MEDICINE MAN

Here is the menu for now. I will add more things as lawyers come into play. Items can cause long term damage, and hurt defense at the same time.

*NOTE* You cant keep any bottles except for the one that you can buy for 5 points.

(in points)

MARKET
1: bandaid. Will help with minor cuts and bleeding.
1: water (fills up a bottle). Can use only once. Will stop your stuffy nose.
2: rock. Can be used to cut. Can be used three times before it loses worth.
3: large rock. Can be used to cut, or to throw. To throw adds +3. To cut, it can be used four times.
4: dirt. Can cause stuffy nose. Nobody knows how. Effects may vary.
4: itching powder. Will cause itchiness.
5: bottle. Anyone on your team can use it, but only one person at a time. Can hold water.
5: stick. You can carve this.
5: very large rock. You can carve this. You can throw this and inflict +5 damage to your regular attack. You can't cut with it, though.
7: lessons. You can learn how to make things.
8: spyware. No burgular can get your things.
9: anti-spyware. Fixes that problem for burgulars.
10: Discount. By one thing, get one free. Works for a week for your entire group.
15: Neosporin. No more cuts will effect you or your team, but large cuts still will.
20: Upgrade. You receive enough points and status abilities to attain a locked position.
25: Upgrade with benefits. You get your old benefits, and the new benefits of your upgrade.

Medicine man:

5: cast. On the offchance someone's rock breaks your bones.
7: cough syrup. Use when you are sick, but only once. Can fill up a bottle.
10: Renew life. Only to be used for bodyguards. Somebody is going to have to pay for it...
20: Surgery. Completely fix your status.

Judging

The points will be graded as follows:

New idea for hidden enemy: /25
Tileset: /15
Object Placement: /10
Funness: /25
Addictiveness: /25

Not annoying: MULTIPLY THE SCORE BY A NUMBER 1-10

So, if you make it at all annoying, you can't even reach 900/1000.
I just want to make sure I dont get junk.

Rules

Keep it simple:

1. Dont make it annoying
2. Submit your map(s) on time. You may have up to two, at this point.
3. Be cautious. I get annoyed quickly.
4. Hidden mines near the ends of levels: Basically an automatic zero, unless if that is the theme.
5. At least three enemies need to be hidden, and they can be revealed throughout the level
...whatever. I'll just mark off if I feel that the hidden enemies dont add enough to the map. carry on.

...

2. Demo length needs to be between 100 and 9,582 frames. Any more, or any less, and you need to ask my approval. Anything above 11,111, I will say no to almost surely, so try to find a semi short one.
3. Make a map off of it in which my demo works as an agd. You need to have at least ten peices of gold. You CAN make a dda, but I will probably not like it, so try to stick with playable maps.
4. Link the map with the original demo data on it and submit it to Numa.
5. Make one of the tags "iwuvturtlez"
6. Post a link to the new map on this topic.
7. Wait to be judged.

Judging:
The scoring will be as follows:

How my demo looks in the map: ?/25
How fun it is for me to play: ?/50
Tileset/Overall look: ?/15
Originalty: ?/8
Map name: ?/2
Total: ?/100

Yes, map name. I will not change that.
Also, the originality refers to how different it is to the other maps.

OMG
NEXT POST I MAKE WILL HAVE SCOREZ

Okay, he has said head, and he has said heart.

In spanish, head is feminine, and heart is masculine.
Cabeza y Corazon. Forget accents, if neccessary. I forget.

in the middle of head is 'be,' and in the middle of heart is 'a'
switch around, and you get 'Abe,' or short for the 16th president of the united states, Abraham Lincoln.
Now then, 16 is four squared, but abraham lincoln was not square, so we have to go to the golf term "fore." Now then, in golf, when you say "fore," you are generally making a big shot. If you get one under par, that is a birdie. There are many kinds of birdies, but many are also extinct. Take the passenger pidgeon. It was doing very well until it got hunted down. Thousands of them were shot. Lincoln was shot, too. Now then, if you are hunting a bird and want to kill it, where do you shoot? Either the head or the heart. La cabeza o el corazon. So, basically, this is just one huge cycle and we should all give up. Right? Naw, i dont think I should get political with this...

For this new competition, you need to make three maps in order to enter. The judging will take me forever, but read before you leave.

You need to first make a map. Make it quite easy. Then you must make another map using the same style, and a similar, but different tileset. I dont want to see you just moving it up one and to the right one or anything. It needs to be completely different, but in a similar style. It also needs to be a bit harder. Mak an even harder map with the same style but different tileset for the third map. The maps, if possible, must be submitted to Numa by, according to Numa time, the end of January.

RULES
1. You must make three maps
2. The tilesets must be similar, but you cannot copy the tileset and paste it on a different part.
3. The difficulty MUST be easy, medium, then hard.
4. All maps must have the tag (turtle-is-hot)
5. The first map must have an enmy other than a mine
6. You must add gold, and the difficulty for all gold must also increase
7. You must not say must as much as I must
8. ...your maps must be turned in by....


Judging:

Overall theme (concept): X/20
Overall theme (execution): X/20
Easiest to hardest is very distinguishable: X/20
Tileset changes are noticeable, but are still similar: X/20
Tileset works well with the theme: X20

FOR EACH MAP (so this will be graded three times)

Funness: X/50
Looks nice: X/10
Addictiveness (do I want to play it again?): X/20
Originality: X/20

Total: X/400

So, good luck to all who join.

Oh? You want to be a judge? Send me an appliation (just reply here, my PM box is getting more full due to other things I am hosting), and see if I like you enough. If not, I will judge myself.

How about this, right after you come home, just don't touch the computer. Or any other procrastinator. How? Easy. Okay. Just when you think Turtle's out of ideas for competitions, it hits you.

Turtle's not.

Now then, if any of you want to take part in a contest with which you have even the slightest chance, this is not the competition for you. In fact, if I was you, I'd skip this entire paragraph and get to the point. Which is where the competition begins.

Now, then. I was sipping a cup of tea (called chai in my native tongue, no, not the chai you get at starbucks, it's pronounced chah-eee) when it hit me. My love left me. I was in dismay. I had no idea what I could do. Then, it hit me, nearly as hard as it hit you.

Turtle's back.

Oh, right, the competition.

Basically, what you have to do is make one map. You can make up to seven. However, if you make seven, they need to all flow. Very well. Because, the judging is as follows:
Spoiler: JUDGING/30 Storyline
/30 Map goes along with story well
/30 Map is fun to play
/10 One extra point for how many times I played it...up to ten

YOU WILL BE DOCKED POINTS FOR BAD NAMES, NOT FOLLOWING RULES, OR OVERALL HATRED OF TURTLES (among other things, like annoying launchpads or enemies, bad placement, etc)

YOU WILL ALSO BE DOCKED POINTS IF I THINK YOU ARE TRYING TO SUCK UP TO ME IN ANY WAY.


I am the only Judge

Storyline? Oh, right. I have a B+ in English, and an A in all of my other classes, so I want to grade your writing. You are to make one map, or two. Or up to seven. And write a story to go along with each of them. Or it. Depending on how it is. However, there are a few rules:
Spoiler: RULES1. You must submit your map to Numa. That way I can tell if the description would fit or not.
2. You must make a map.
3. You must give your map a good name.
4. You must give your map a tag. This is the tag it must have: turtlewuv
5. You must tattletale on everyone who does not follow a rule. Each tattle gives you an extra five points.
6. You must figure out whether or not #5 is a lie...or must you?
7. You must make the storyline flow if you make more than one map.
8. You must make the maps flow if you make more than one map.
9. You must make the map fun.
10. MAKE TURTLE STOP SAYING MUST...

(nevermind that)

Prizes are as follows:
If over ten people join, then your prizes will look like this:
First place: A dedication, a map kind of your choice, not DDA.
Second place: A dedication, probably just a five second map.
Third place: Absolutely nothing.
Fourth place: A dedication to you laughing at third place.

If there are over fifteen, then twenty, then twenty five, etc. entries, then the prizes will be better. So invite your friends, neighbors, and kitties to join in.

Quote: Nexx, June 11, 2008 02:36 pm
Personally, I'm for option 2 - whole numbers for placing votes, whole numbers + .5's for viewing the average rating. It keeps placing a vote simple and also gives a sufficient amount of tiers for displaying average ratings.

For placing votes, I suppose it's largely a matter of personal preference, but for viewing averages, there are logical arguments for a system that includes .5's.

With nearly a hundred thousand maps on NUMA (taking into account deleted maps), we need more than 6 levels total (particularly since there's only 3 levels for "above average" maps). A current rating of 4 spans a huge range of quality, from just above 3.5 (7/10) to just below 4.5 (9/10). (That's obvious, I know, but by making the obvious explicit, I am hopefully getting some people to see the problem for what it is.)

Chase has cited Newgrounds as a good example and I whole-heartedly agree with that. Newgrounds rates in whole numbers and displays the average rating to two decimal points. Since most maps only get a handful of votes, two decimal points is obviously overkill, but given the quantity of maps on NUMA, using only whole numbers lumps things together far too much.

So that's my opinion. What say you all?

Gives a sufficient amount of tiers? There are enough! Why would you need more? Just so you could whine about being sniped, or have your ratings mean more? I don't see a purpose to it.

Yes, a huge range of quality, but now you won't be biased seeing a 3.5 map and a 4.5 map and automatically thinking the 4.5 is that much better. It isn't. Not neccessarily. Chances are the only difference is that one was made by a top rated author, while the other wasn't. Just making the incriments smaller makes people care more about ratings.

Spoiler: So, what the heck do I have to do to get that many dedications?Each contest will be themed.
You have one week to submit your maps, no matter what. So, if you want to get everything over with, you can submit all of your maps in the same week, so you won't have to worry about it. Or you could take the preferrable route, and go along with the competition. So your first map is due on July 19. The next map will probably be due some time in early August, then it should be relatively standard after that, unless school takes forever.

Theme for week one: Must use at least one jump pad for every sixteen squares used, rounded up. Also, use a creative tileset.

Judging:
Launchpad Concentration (not too much or too little): x/5
Tileset: x/55
Fun: x/40
Total: x/100 (to pass, x must equal 60)

Theme for week two (in case anyone will be gone): The only acceptable enemies, including mines, are chaingun drones and laser drones. There must be useful trap doors, as well as multiple doors to exit the level from.

Judging:
Tileset: X/20
Route 1 Fun: X/40
Route 2 Fun: X/40
If you use more than two different doors to exit from, I will just divide it as equally as possible between the routes. No more than five routes will be acceptable.
Total: x/100 (to pass, x must equal 65)

(Just so you know, x will go from 60, 65, 70, 70, 75, 80, 80, 85, 90, 90, 95, 95, (and 95 will continue if there are enough people who manage to amaze me consistantly))
Spoiler: Rules1. Submit your map to Numa
2. PM me the link to your map, and THE SUBJECT OF THE PM MUST BE 'Dictator Week _', the _ referring to whichever week you are submitting it for.
3. Follow the theme
4. IN ORDER TO QUALIFY FOR A PRIZE, you must pass at least three weeks (70). In order to qualify for five or more dedications, you must pass at least eight weeks (85). In order to qualify for ten or more dedications, you need to reach a total of 95 points at least seven weeks (not neccessarily consecutively).
5. If you EVER get 100/100, you get two deds added to your final prize. If you get it twice, you will get a total of six deds added. If you get it three times, you get a total of fourteen deds added on to your final. If you get it four times, you get a total of thirty deds added on to your final. I'm confident you won't get more, based off of the themes I have in mind.
Spoiler: In conlusionIf this works well enough, in the end, when there are only a few people left, I will make the themes a lot more specific and difficult.

Quote: wilderness, August 17, 2008 12:32 pm
Quote: LittleViking, August 17, 2008 01:12 pm
It's all fades into the background.
Well, for me this was the entire point of the movie.
The first movie we see Batman's emergence, the second we see the repercussions of his actions: the birth of the Joker.
Consider two things:
1. These are origin stories, stripped back and (regardless of how effectively you think it's been achieved) re-built.
2. The Joker is Batman's inevitable balance.
TDK is the story of the rise of the Joker and the affect it had on the people of Gotham, Batman included. That he shadows the events surrounding him is integral to his character. As an antithesis, just as the people of Gotham rise up to stand for the hope that Batman represents for them, the chaos that surrounds the Joker sucks like a whirlpool and spits out the bodies.

That some of the films story arcs feel like by-products is because they are just that: the remains left in the Joker's wake.
At least, that's what I took from it. I found the the experience immensely satisfying.

If I could only write that well for my English teachers...

Well put
